18769-the-autobiography-of-a-play-papers.title: The Autobiography of a Play
18769-the-autobiography-of-a-play-papers.creator: Bronson Howard
18769-the-autobiography-of-a-play-papers.description: A book by Bronson Howard. It happens that one of my own plays has had a very curious history. It has appeared before the American public in two forms, so radically different that a description of the changes made, and of the reasons for making them, will involve the consideration of some very interesting laws of dramatic construction.

arxiv-2008-02801.title: Exact Solutions of the Time Derivative Fokker-Planck Equation: A Novel Approach
arxiv-2008-02801.creator: H. I. Abdel-Gawad 1 ∗ , N. H. Sweilam 1 , S. M. AL − - Mekhlafi 2 , D. Baleanu 3,4
arxiv-2008-02801.description: Abstract Abstract: In the present article, an approach to find the exact solution of the fractional Fokker-Planck equation is presented. It is based on transforming it to a system of first-order partial differential equation via Hopf transformation, together with implementing the extended unified method. On the other hand, reduction of the fractional derivatives to non autonomous ordinary derivative.

arxiv-2101-04599.title: Superconductivity and strong anharmonicity in novel Nb-S phases
arxiv-2101-04599.creator: Roman Lucrezi, Christoph Heil
arxiv-2101-04599.description: Abstract In this work we explore the phase diagram of the binary Nb-S system from ambient pressures up to 250 GPa 250\text{\,}\mathrm{GPa} using ab initio evolutionary crystal structure prediction. We find several new stable compositions and phases, especially in the high-pressure regime, and investigate their electronic, vibrational, and superconducting properties.

arxiv-2206-02984.title: Lindbladian Many-Body Localization
arxiv-2206-02984.creator: Ryusuke Hamazaki, Masaya Nakagawa, Taiki Haga, Masahito Ueda
arxiv-2206-02984.description: Abstract We discover a novel localization transition that alters the dynamics of coherence in disordered many-body spin systems subject to Markovian dissipation. The transition occurs in the middle spectrum of the Lindbladian super-operator whose eigenstates obey the universality of non-Hermitian random-matrix theory for weak disorder and exhibit localization of off-diagonal degrees of freedom for strong disorder.

arxiv-2310-14464.title: A Cryptographic Perspective on the Verifiability of Quantum Advantage
arxiv-2310-14464.creator: Nai-Hui Chia, Honghao Fu, Fang Song, Penghui Yao
arxiv-2310-14464.description: Abstract In recent years, achieving verifiable quantum advantage on a NISQ device has emerged as an important open problem in quantum information. The sampling-based quantum advantages are not known to have efficient verification methods. This paper investigates the verification of quantum advantage from a cryptographic perspective.

arxiv-2402-06025.title: Doing Experiments and Revising Rules with Natural Language and Probabilistic Reasoning
arxiv-2402-06025.creator: Top Piriyakulkij (wp237@cornell.edu), Kevin Ellis (kellis@cornell.edu)
arxiv-2402-06025.description: Abstract We build a computational model of how humans actively infer hidden rules by doing experiments. The basic principles behind the model is that, even if the rule is deterministic, the learner considers a broader space of fuzzy probabilistic rules, which it represents in natural language, and updates its hypotheses online after each experiment according to approximately Bayesian principles.

arxiv-2405-19383.title: Network Analytics for Anti-Money Laundering – A Systematic Literature Review and Experimental Evaluation
arxiv-2405-19383.creator: Bruno Deprez, Toon Vanderschueren, Bart Baesens, Tim Verdonck, Wouter Verbeke
arxiv-2405-19383.description: Abstract Money laundering presents a pervasive challenge, burdening society by financing illegal activities. The use of network information is increasingly being explored to effectively combat money laundering, given it involves connected parties. This led to a surge in research on network analytics for anti-money laundering (AML). The literature is, however, fragmented and a comprehensive overview of existing work is missing.

arxiv-2502-11284.title: Balancing the Budget: Understanding Trade-offs Between Supervised and Preference-Based Finetuning
arxiv-2502-11284.creator: Mohit Raghavendra, Junmo Kang, Alan Ritter
arxiv-2502-11284.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Mohit Raghavendra, Junmo Kang, Alan Ritter. Post-training of Large Language Models often involves a pipeline of Supervised Finetuning (SFT) followed by Preference Finetuning (PFT) using methods like Direct Preference Optimization. Both stages require annotated data that are very different in structure and costs. We study how to optimally allocate a fixed training data budget between the two stages, through extensive experiments spanning four diverse tasks, multiple model sizes and various data annotation costs.

arxiv-2509-10514.title: A Differential Manifold Perspective and Universality Analysis of Continuous Attractors in Artificial Neural Networks Journal: Neural Networks
arxiv-2509-10514.creator: Shaoxin Tian, Hongkai Liu, Yuying Yang, Jiali Yu, Zizheng Miao, Xuming Huang, Zhishuai Liu, Zhang Yi
arxiv-2509-10514.description: Abstract Continuous attractors are critical for information processing in both biological and artificial neural systems, with implications for spatial navigation, memory, and deep learning optimization. However, existing research lacks a unified framework to analyze their properties across diverse dynamical systems, limiting cross-architectural generalizability.

arxiv-2512-02175.title: Sampling on Metric Graphs
arxiv-2512-02175.creator: Rajat Vadiraj Dwaraknath & Lexing Ying
arxiv-2512-02175.description: Abstract Metric graphs are structures obtained by associating edges in a standard graph with segments of the real line and gluing these segments at the vertices of the graph. The resulting structure has a natural metric that allows for the study of differential operators and stochastic processes on the graph.

arxiv-2512-08061.title: LUNA: Linear Universal Neural Attention with Generalization Guarantees
arxiv-2512-08061.creator: Ashkan Shahbazi, Ping He, Ali Abbasi, [0.3em] Yikun Bai, Xinran Liu, Elaheh Akbari, [0.3em] Darian Salehi, Navid NaderiAlizadeh, Soheil Kolouri, [0.8em] Department of Computer Science, Vanderbilt University, Nashville, TN, USA, [0.2em] Department of Electrical & Computer Engineering, Vanderbilt Univ
arxiv-2512-08061.description: Abstract Scaling attention faces a critical bottleneck: the 𝒪 ⁡ ( n 2 ) \mathcal{O}(n^{2}) quadratic computational cost of softmax attention, which limits its application in long-sequence domains. While linear attention mechanisms reduce this cost to 𝒪 ⁡ ( n ) \mathcal{O}(n) , they typically rely on fixed random feature maps, such as random Fourier features or hand-crafted functions.

pmc-10595675.title: Barriers to the effective implementation of One health policies against AMR in the EU
pmc-10595675.creator: M Dates, M Davies
pmc-10595675.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Funded by the EU4Health 2021 Programme, Tetra Tech conducted a study for the European Commission on the “Barriers to the effective implementation of policies against antimicrobial resistance (AMR)” in the EU Member States, Norway and Iceland. The study provides input to support the EU's overall goal to combat AMR by improving the development and implementation of One Health national action plans (NAPs) which, in turn, shall contain effective measures in infection prevention and control and prudent use of antimicrobials.

pmc-11709611.title: Exploring selective neuronal vulnerability in Alzheimer’s disease – key pathways are downregulated in vulnerable subpopulations of RORB and CDH9 excitatory neurons of the entorhinal cortex at Braak 0
pmc-11709611.creator: Alexander V Soloviev, Felipe Luiz Pereira, Renata Elaine Paraizo Leite, Claudia Kimie Suemoto, Kun Leng, Martin Kampmann, Lea T Grinberg
pmc-11709611.description: BackgroundUnderstanding the molecular mechanisms underlying selective neuronal vulnerability is crucial for developing effective treatments for Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Our group has shown that RORB/CDH9‐positive excitatory neurons in the entorhinal cortex (EC) display selective vulnerability as early as Braak stage (BB) 2. However, not all RORB/CDH9‐positive neurons are vulnerable.

pmc-12495638.title: Tubacin alleviate the reproductive toxicity of deoxynivalenol in mouse oocytes and zygotes via strengthening microtubule stability
pmc-12495638.creator: Hui Luo, Jianhua Chen, Zhihan Guo, Yanyan Zhu, Yipin Wang, Tian Wu, Siyue Yin, Cao Li, Youqiang Su, Yao Chen, Yun Qian, Congxiu Miao, Ruizhi Feng
pmc-12495638.description: Deoxynivalenol (DON) is one of the most common food contaminants, widely present in grain products. Studies using murine and porcine models show deoxynivalenol exposure impairs oocyte maturation and mitochondrial function; however, the exact mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we demonstrate that DON exposure markedly altered the microtubule nucleation-associated protein expression in oocytes.

pmc-12577307.title: Genetically encoded biosensor enabled mining, characterisation and engineering of aromatic acid MFS transporters
pmc-12577307.creator: Philip Le Roy, Micaela Chacόn, Neil Dixon
pmc-12577307.description: Active transport of chemical species across the cell membrane represents a critical biological and biotechnological function, allowing the cell to selectively import compounds of nutritional value whilst exporting potentially toxic compounds. Major facilitator superfamily (MFS) transporters represent a ubiquitous class able to uptake and export an array of different chemical species.

pmc-13276865.title: Conservative Management of Breast Implant-Associated Infections: Identifying Risk Factors for Failure
pmc-13276865.creator: Idoia Bilbao, María Pascual, Miguel Sogbe, Francisco Carmona-Torre, Trinidad Baselga, Manuel Pina, Iñigo Pineda, José Ramón Yuste, José L del Pozo
pmc-13276865.description: Background. Breast implant-associated infections remain a challenging complication, with limited high-quality evidence to guide management. Implant removal is often considered the standard approach, although conservative strategies aimed at implant salvage may be successful in selected patients. We conducted a retrospective observational study of 42 patients diagnosed with breast implant-associated infection at a tertiary hospital between 2000 and 2024.
